newsitem.title: ITALY: Rome cabinet approves draft law on STET transfer.
newsitem.headline: Rome cabinet approves draft law on STET transfer.

text.p: The Italian cabinet approved a draft law on Wednesday to complete transfer of telecommunications giant STET from state holdings concern IRI to the Treasury.

The draft law aims to counter the effects of a government defeat last week, when the lower house of parliament voted against the transfer, which is necessary for STET's planned privatisation later this year.

The draft law confirms that the Treasury will not have to launch a public offering for STET. It also sets up special tax exemption provisions connected to the privatisation of STET, a cabinet statement said.
STET's sale is required under a 1992 agreement between the European Commission and Italy to reduce IRI's huge debt in return for allowing state subsidies to IRI and its subsidiaries.

The agreement obliges IRI to cut its debt by 19 trillion lire by the end of June by selling STET and privatising motorway operating company Autostrade, publishing company Seat and shipping firm Finmare.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government lost the vote on a STET decree last week after the hard-left Communist Refoundation abstained in the Chamber of Deputies.
Prodi's government must rely on Communist Refoundation's 35 deputies to pass legislation in the lower house.
